frames.narration: A browser in Berlin needs img.example.com/hero.jpg. The CDN's DNS answers with the address of the Frankfurt PoP, chosen from where the resolver is and which PoPs are healthy.

The browser opens HTTPS to the PoP. The PoP holds the certificate for img.example.com, so the handshake needs one round trip of about 12 ms. The cache key is built from the host, the path and the Accept-Encoding header named in Vary.

The copy at the PoP expired a moment ago, so this is a miss. The PoP asks its regional shield. Forty more requests for the same file arrive during the next 150 ms, and they wait for this one fetch instead of starting their own.

The shield also holds an expired copy, with its ETag. It sends a conditional request to the origin over a connection that is already open, so there is no new handshake. The round trip to Virginia takes about 90 ms.
The file has not changed, so the origin answers 304 Not Modified with no body: 300 bytes instead of 180 KB. The shield renews its copy for another hour (max-age=3600).
The shield sends the 180 KB image to the PoP, which stores it and answers all 41 waiting users. The first one waited about 150 ms. The origin handled one request for 41 users.
A little later a neighbour asks for the same file. The PoP has a fresh copy and answers at once, in about 25 ms. The origin is not involved.
The company replaces the image and calls the purge API with the surrogate key for it. The purge is published to every PoP and shield, and within about two seconds each marks its copy as expired.
The next request is a miss that fetches the new version, with a new ETag. The user waits about 150 ms once; everyone after them gets the new image from the cache.
